title: Nets, Solids and Euler's Formula
summary: Faces, edges and vertices, the 11 nets of a cube, and a formula that works for every polyhedron.

cbse.chapter: Ganita Prakash Part 2 Ch 4: Exploring Some Geometric Themes
Earlier NCERT Ch 13: Visualising Solid Shapes

objectives: I can describe solids by their faces, edges and vertices.
I can tell whether a net folds into a cube.
I can use Euler's formula F + V − E = 2.
misconceptions: Any 6 squares joined together make a cube.
A cylinder has edges like a cuboid.
Euler's formula only works for cubes.
